newsitem.title: ITALY: Versace ashes arrive back in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Versace ashes arrive back in Italy.

text.p: A private plane carrying the ashes of slain Italian fashion designer Gianni Versace arrived at an airport in the northern city of Bergamo from Miami on Friday, airport officials said.

"The plane arrived a few minutes ago," an air traffic control official told Reuters. He said he had seen several people get out of the plane, but could not confirm they were the designer's family. The ashes were due to be taken by helicopter to the lakeside town of Como, where Versace had a villa.
The family was expected to hold a private service at the villa during the weekend and a memorial mass in Milan cathedral early next week.

Versace, 50, was shot dead on Tuesday on the steps of his Miami Beach mansion. Police have mounted a massive manhunt for Andrew Cunanan, a 27-year-old homosexual prostitute whom they describe as their only suspect in the murder.
Versace's brother Santo, the commercial brains behind the fashion empire, and his sister Donatella, herself a talented designer, said on Thursday they would continue the business.

The family apparently decided to land in Bergamo, just east of Milan to avoid an army of reporters and television cameras hoping to catch a glimpse of the homecoming. They had earlier appealed to the media to respect their privacy.
